newsitem.title: UK: BP seeks permission for new power plant.
newsitem.headline: BP seeks permission for new power plant.

text.p: British Petroleum Co Plc said on Monday it was seeking permission for a gas-fired power station to be built at one of its petrochemical plant sites in south Wales.
At the same time, the oil company is looking for a partner to build and operate the 1,100 MW station and make the necessary investments, a spokesman said.
Building the plant would cost approximately 300 million stg.
"But BP will not be putting money into this," the spokesman said. "This deal more than anything is a land deal (rather than a move into electricity by BP)," he added.
Most of the electricity generated by the planned power plant is scheduled to be sold in the wholesale market or to large industrial users rather than be used by BP's own operations.
BP said in August it wanted to build a similar 1,100 power station at its Saltend chemical complex near Hull in the north-east of England.
The plant there is to be operated by Entergy Corp of the U.S.

Unlike the station near Hull, the power station in Wales will not necessarily take BP gas, the BP spokesman said. "The Hull project is very much tied in with BP Exploration, but the south Wales project is not like that," he said.
